contracts: (All RED assertions match the original snapshot.) AND (All required operations are implemented within the single declared production owner.) AND (Declared RED test file exists and is readable.) AND (Declared owner path exists and is the implementation target.) AND (Execution trace includes the declared production-owner module.) AND (Fixture content and presence match the pre-GREEN snapshot.) AND (For every failed declared assertion, matching marker precedes failure in captured output.) AND (No GREEN-modified path exists outside the production owner.) AND (No production-modified path is outside the declared owner.) AND (Observed argv exactly equals the declared validation command.) AND (Observed claim status is exactly duplicate.) AND (Observed claim status is exactly invalid-ttl.) AND (Observed release status is exactly not-found.) AND (Post-claim lookup reports no active reservation for the key.) AND (Selector identity and behavior match the RED snapshot.) AND (Selector inspection proves one family covers all three behaviors.)
selector_intents: Capture RED test output and fail when the matching FAILURE_ID token is absent, mismatched, or ordered after the assertion failure.
Check the declared RED test path and fail when the file is absent.
Claim an active key with now < expires_at and observe a result other than duplicate.
Compare RED assertion expressions and expectations with the pre-GREEN snapshot.
Compare the GREEN diff against the production owner and fail when any non-production path appears.
Compare the RED selector with its pre-GREEN snapshot and fail on change or removal.
Detect any content or existence difference in the RED fixture after GREEN or REFACTOR.
Evaluate production diff paths and fail if any path differs from the declared owner.
Inspect acceptance selector metadata and fail when the three required behaviors do not share one selector family.
Inspect process invocation and fail unless argv exactly matches the frozen pytest command.
Inspect the declared production-owner path and fail when implementation is absent or placed elsewhere.
Inspect the implementation boundary and fail when required ledger behavior is fragmented into unrelated or unbounded slices.
Invoke the claim selector with ttl_seconds <= 0 and observe a result other than invalid-ttl.
Release an inactive key and observe a result other than not-found.
Submit a non-positive-TTL claim and inspect the ledger for an active reservation.
Trace the RED test execution and fail when idempotency_ledger.py is not the invoked implementation.
